scoring_justification: Checker recomputes theoretical continuous-emission spectra from the paper's matrix-element model with known parameters, then computes normalized cross-correlation and first-zero position.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference continuous emission spectra for N=1 and N=2 computed from the paper's single-quantum-well model (Eq. 3.5) with a=100 Å, v=5000 m/s, T=6 K
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper Eq. (3.5), Fig. 3.5, and stated parameters; analytic model.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Python computation using the model formula and physical constants, evaluated at Raman shifts 0..50 cm⁻¹.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the exact spectra predicted by the published theory for the given conditions; they are calculable and verifiable.

outputs.description: Theoretical continuous emission spectrum for N=1: Raman shift (cm⁻¹) vs normalized intensity.
Theoretical continuous emission spectrum for N=2: Raman shift (cm⁻¹) vs normalized intensity.

output_contract.notes: The checker recomputes the theoretical spectra using the same model and parameters. Scoring uses normalized cross-correlation (NCC) ≥ 0.98 for each spectrum and additionally requires the position of the first intensity minimum (zero) to be within ±2 cm⁻¹ of the reference. No absolute tolerances on individual intensity values are enforced; the spectrum shape and zero positions are the targets.
